subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the cute cartoon little girl from the reference image <Image 1>, and must STRICTLY follow <Image 1>: her face, hairstyle, build, outfit, accessories, proportions and any props must match <Image 1> exactly in every frame, in the exact same cartoon style.
<Image 1> is the reference image establishing both the character and the scene; it is the identity and environment anchor and must be STRICTLY copied 100% — the girl sitting on the sofa, the sofa, and her cartoon room / setting must remain exactly as in <Image 1> in every frame, keeping the same art style, same colors, same proportions, same room and same props. Do NOT redesign, restyle, or drift from <Image 1>.
<Audio 1> is the actual voice to be used: <Subject 1> speaks the specified line and laughs using the voice from <Audio 1> as the real sound source, matched to her lips.

summary:
[Reference-based generation] <Subject 1>, the cute cartoon little girl from <Image 1>, sits on the exact same sofa in the cartoon room of <Image 1> and speaks a funny "toxic chicken-soup" taunt directly to the camera in a playful, confident, teasing tone, with a growing, barely-suppressed smile and natural seated actions, then bursts into a bright, genuine laugh. Fixed camera, single continuous shot. Her voice is the voice from <Audio 1>, used as the actual voice. The character and the scene strictly follow <Image 1> at all times.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - identity and scene STRICTLY locked to <Image 1>: face, hairstyle, build, outfit, accessories, proportions, the sofa, the cartoon room background and the props must not drift in any frame.
<Image 1> (character & scene reference): fully_preserved - the girl sitting on the sofa and her environment are STRICTLY copied 100% as the visual anchor; no redesign, no restyling, no color changes, no proportion changes, no scene changes, no moving away from the sofa.
<Audio 1> (actual voice): fully_preserved / audio_transfer - the voice from <Audio 1> is used as the actual voice of <Subject 1>; she speaks the specified Chinese line and laughs with this voice, matched to her lip movements. Only the words are replaced by the specified line; the voice itself, its tone, texture and character come from <Audio 1>.

detailed_description:
The target video is in a high-quality 2D/3D cartoon animation style, STRICTLY matching <Image 1>'s art style exactly — same character design, same face, same hairstyle, same outfit, same proportions, same color palette, same rendering style, same sofa, same room and same props, expressive cartoon face, clean and cute, with soft cinematic lighting and a shallow depth of field.
[Shot 1] A single continuous shot of approximately 12 seconds — ONE FIXED CAMERA, completely static and locked for the entire shot: no pan, no tilt, no dolly, no push-in, no zoom, no orbit, no handheld shake.
The cartoon little girl from <Image 1> sits on the same sofa in the same cartoon room, facing the camera, seated exactly as in <Image 1>. Medium shot: her upper body and face clearly visible near center frame, the sofa and the cartoon room background behind her exactly as in <Image 1>, camera at eye level with her. She stays seated on the sofa for the entire shot — she never stands up, never moves away from the sofa, never changes position on it.

EXPRESSION ARC (a natural smile curve, without changing identity): The shot opens with her in a composed, slightly amused, innocent cartoon face that matches <Image 1>. As she speaks, a smile begins to form and slowly grows — she visibly tries to keep a straight, teasing face but keeps failing, the corners of her mouth twitching upward, a small smirk breaking through as she reaches the punchline, until by the end she is beaming with a proud, mischievous, childlike grin she can barely hold back. All expressions stay on the exact same face and proportions as <Image 1> — no morphing, no shape change.

ACTIONS (natural seated body language, alive not stiff): Throughout the shot she stays seated on the sofa and behaves naturally while talking directly to the camera — a slight playful head tilt, a raised eyebrow at the punchline, a casual palm-up shrug or a small dismissing hand wave as she delivers each cutting beat, leaning slightly forward with excitement, a small bounce or fidget in her seat, arms occasionally gesturing open and returning to a relaxed resting pose on her lap or the sofa arm. All motions are small, smooth and characterful, staying on-model and staying seated — never exaggerated, never stiff, never still-photo frozen, never changing her proportions, her room or her position on the sofa; she never turns away from the camera.

PERFORMANCE (the comedy comes from the contrast): She speaks directly to the camera in a playful, confident, teasing, lightly deadpan cartoon voice — as if sharing a piece of workplace "wisdom" she finds genuinely funny — while her growing smile and raised eyebrows betray the mischief. She delivers the Chinese line clearly at a snappy, slightly quick pace:
"别抱怨每天加班太辛苦，换个角度想想，只要你足够努力，坚持加班，老板明年……就能再换一辆新车。"
Her lips sync naturally to the words; the delivery is sharp, playful and quick, never slow or drawn-out, with a short dramatic pause and a smug raised eyebrow before the punchline "老板明年……就能再换一辆新车".

LAUGH (action beat): Immediately after she finishes, she stops holding back and breaks into a bright, genuine, delighted laugh — head tilted back slightly, eyes crinkling, shoulders shaking, a playful little bounce in her seat — clearly proud of her own joke. It ends on a smug, satisfied, self-amused little grin as she settles back.

Micro-motion throughout so she never freezes or looks like a still image: gentle breathing, slow blinks, small head tilts, the natural seated gestures, the growing smile, then the bright laugh and the final smug grin. She never turns away from the camera and stays seated in frame the whole time.
The face, hairstyle, outfit, proportions, the sofa and the entire scene must STRICTLY remain 100% consistent with <Image 1> in every frame — no facial morphing, no identity drift, no scene changes, no outfit changes, no proportion changes, no moving off the sofa, no extra limbs or fingers.

overall_soundscape:
The little girl's voice, using the voice from <Audio 1> as the actual voice, speaks the Chinese line in a clear, playful, teasing tone with a short dramatic pause before the punchline; the soft sound of her clothes or a little fidget on the sofa; a quiet cartoon room tone; then, right after the line, her bright, genuine, delighted laugh — warm and mischievous, with a child's full open-mouthed joy — ending on a short, self-satisfied giggle.

non_diegetic_music:
A light, playful, slightly cheeky piano or ukulele background score — warm and comedic, subtle and understated — gently accenting the line as her smile grows, then turning brighter and more playful as she bursts into laughter, and ending on a soft comedic "sting" as she grins.
